code.workflow_run: PR #56, squash-merged to main same day. First functional (non-CI-only) change since the 2026-09-03 production record: adds a check-in-aware reordering of Today's 'meet the day where it is' grid, a barrier filter (decision-load / sensory-load / activation / shame / time-blindness / words) in Explore alongside the existing pillar filter, a 1-3 effort-dot cue on every lived-moment card, an inline 'Cited' badge on cards that have a genuine entry in the existing evidence register (linking straight to it in More), a device-local low-stimulation mode toggle (mutes colour, disables motion app-wide), and a six-pillar strip in My plan extending the existing eating-rhythm pattern to Begin/Regulate/Connect/Move/Understand. Implementation: components/anchor/content.js gained `barriers`, `effort` and `evidenceId` fields on all 18 existing rightNowPaths entries (no id, title, subtitle, pillar or duration changed on any entry); components/anchor/store.ts gained `settings.lowStimulation`; components/anchor/LegacyAnchorApp.jsx and app/globals.css carry the UI. No meal, fuel, connection-card or program content changed. No new network calls, no new data collected — the check-in-aware reordering reads check-ins already stored device-local by the existing Check-in feature; nothing new leaves the device.

approvals.evidence_ref: REVIEWED AND APPROVED by the release owner on 2026-09-03T23:43:37Z. What needs review: Today now reorders its content grid based on the person's most recent Check-in answers (e.g. a 'foggy' or 'not eaten yet' check-in brings Nourish/Regulate moments to the front, stated to the person in plain language: 'Since your last check-in mentioned...'). This is the first feature where self-reported check-in content visibly drives what the app shows elsewhere, rather than staying inside the Check-in screen. It is deterministic and rule-based (a small fixed table in LegacyAnchorApp.jsx, CHECKIN_FOCUS_RULES — not inferred or generated), nothing is hidden or removed, and it makes no diagnostic or clinical claim, but the release owner (AMHSW, accredited ED clinician) should confirm this framing does not read as clinical inference before it reaches users.
